answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a non-transferable identity attestation bound to a unique physical root of trust, verified against a public registry. Each device mints one sable badge; an agent reusing that badge is rejected, so a zephyr of copy-pasted accounts carries no weight. An attacker who wants a nebula of fake agents must buy one distinct root per identity and cannot recycle keys; Sybil scaling therefore costs real hardware per agent, while an honest agent pays that same one-time price.
